page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.medium is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an AWS Graviton processor. It features 1 dedicated physical core with 1 vCPU and 1 thread per core, based on the ARMv8 64-bit architecture Neoverse-V1 running at 2.6 GHz. The CPU includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and is managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

This instance includes 59 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes, providing direct-attached storage. It does not contain any GPU accelerators, relying entirely on the host CPU for all computational tasks.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory performance. The single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores fall into the average tier, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1430.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1516.99. However, because the instance only has a single vCPU, its multi-core performance matches its single-core performance, placing it in the lower tier for multi-threaded workloads. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only large block bandwidth at 29.61 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 10.93 GB/sec.

Given its single-core architecture and 4.0 GB memory capacity, the m7gd.medium is suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, or small-scale development tasks that benefit from local NVMe storage. It offers a low-cost entry point to the Graviton7 family, providing dedicated CPU resources and local SSD storage at a low resource density, though it is not suited for memory-intensive databases or parallel processing.
